sources.entry: onUI - Open-source browser extension and MCP server for annotation-first UI pair programming with AI agents. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot. Chrome, Edge, Firefox. Free, GPL-3.0.

summary.one_liner: onUI is an open-source browser extension plus local MCP bridge that lets you annotate page elements and regions so AI coding agents can act on them.
summary.what_it_does: Adds a per-tab toggle browser extension for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox that injects an annotation toolbar into web pages without changing app code. Users can hover and click elements, or hold Shift to batch-select several, then attach intent and severity in a shared dialog. A draw mode lets users mark rectangular or elliptical regions. Annotations can be exported in compact, standard, detailed, or forensic formats, and a local MCP server and native bridge expose them to AI agents. The README says there is no cloud backend, and the UI uses Shadow DOM for style isolation.
use_cases: annotate UI bugs for an AI coding agent
pair program on frontend changes with Claude Code
send page element context to an MCP-connected assistant
mark regions of a web page for visual feedback
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <installer URL from README> | bash  (macOS/Linux; add --firefox for Firefox artifact)
Answer y when prompted to set up the local MCP bridge
Chrome/Edge: open chrome://extensions or edge://extensions, enable Developer mode, Load unpacked, select ~/.onui/extensions/current
notable: Annotation-first workflow: select elements or regions on the live page, then send structured context to AI agents
Per-tab ON/OFF control, off by default
Local-only MCP server and native bridge with no cloud backend required
Auto-registers the onui-local MCP entry for Claude Code and Codex when installed
Release is packaged locally via app.sh with no CI/CD dependency
caveats: Browser support in this release is Chrome stable, Edge stable, and Firefox stable (unpacked) only
MCP setup needs Node 20+ and the repo itself, since @onui/mcp-server is private and workspace-local
Chromium unpacked installs need a manual Load unpacked step
